name: Incorporation Day
description: Observed on March 14th — the anniversary of the 2189 Meridian Charter signing that legally established the city-state of GLMZ under joint corponation governance — Incorporation Day is a mandatory civic celebration enforced by all major employers. Workers receive a half-day productivity bonus if they display corporate livery colors (each corponation has its own assigned hue), and public screens across Tiers 2 through 5 run the famous Vantage-Kulkarni documentary 'We Built This Light.' The holiday was designed by Helix Media's cultural engineering division to replace older national holidays and redirect civic pride toward corporate identity.
cultural_impact: Incorporation Day is one of the few moments the entire city shares a public calendar date, making it a flashpoint for both corporate pageantry and organized dissent — anti-charter graffiti campaigns triple in the weeks leading up to March 14th.
key_figures: DJ Crowbait (the Gray Zone counter-celebration organizer)
locations: Helix Media Broadcast Tower, Tier 4 North
The Scar, Tier 1 the Gray Zone underpass murals
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone archivist uncovers evidence that the 2189 charter was backdated — the real signing happened two years earlier under different, more exploitative terms — and the documentary was edited to hide it.

A player character is hired to protect a corporate parade float, unaware that a the Gray Zone collective has spent eight months engineering a spectacular, non-lethal public humiliation event for this exact date.

A synthetic employee is denied their productivity bonus because their employment classification technically predates the charter — an administrative loophole that affects thousands of synthetics and triggers a landmark legal challenge.
origin_event: The signing of the Meridian Charter on March 14, 2189, which dissolved the last municipal government structures and transferred civic authority to a corponation consortium, formally establishing GLMZ as a corporate city-state.
tier_observations: Tier 1 (the Gray Zone) ignores or actively subverts the holiday with counter-murals, noise protests, and the annual 'Unchartered' ghost market. Tier 2 workers comply minimally — wearing a pin or changing a profile flag — to avoid the wage penalty. Tier 3 treats it as a genuine day off with family gatherings and rooftop viewings of the fireworks. Tier 4 hosts invitation-only brand parties and networking events at corporate lounges. Tier 5 (Spire) attends private charter galas where the real political relationships of the city are negotiated over the holiday's social cover.
